title: Prompt Two phase dependency graph, allocation map, critical path, and parallel frontier
coverage: phases=21/21 measured; edges=32 authored; allocation=13/13 buckets measured; critical_path computed; blocked_now measured; parallel_frontier computed. Deliverable lists are spec-faithful summaries, not verbatim transcriptions - cite the spec_line for exact wording.

relationship_to_dependency_graph_json.verdict: DEPENDENCY-GRAPH.json was NOT modified. This is a SEPARATE, ADDITIVE file.
relationship_to_dependency_graph_json.why: DEPENDENCY-GRAPH.json is not a skeleton. It is a fully machine-derived artifact (103 work-unit nodes, 21 edges) produced by tools/command-center/catalog.py:build_graph, and tools/command-center/validate.py check V-GRAPH asserts the committed file equals build_graph(catalog) by whole-dict equality (validate.py:238-245). That validator runs in CI at .github/workflows/quality.yml:402.
relationship_to_dependency_graph_json.proof: Both-states detector control on a temp COPY via validate.py --graph: STATE A (committed graph) -> V-GRAPH silent, violations=1; STATE B (committed graph + one extra top-level key 'phases') -> V-GRAPH FIRES, violations=2. Detector VALID (silent on control, fires on broken).
relationship_to_dependency_graph_json.consequence: Adding ANY top-level key to DEPENDENCY-GRAPH.json turns a CI gate red. The two graphs are also different objects: DEPENDENCY-GRAPH.json is the WORK-UNIT graph (R-A*/R-B*/R-H*/R-M*), this file is the PHASE graph (0..16). Merging them would fuse two namespaces with different lifecycles.
relationship_to_dependency_graph_json.owner_decision_needed: If the owner wants the phase graph inside DEPENDENCY-GRAPH.json, then catalog.py:build_graph must emit it (so parity holds) - a code change, not a data edit.

measurement_notes.line_numbering_trap: pathlib.Path.read_text() applies universal-newline translation. The spec file is CRLF (29,273 CRLF) AND contains 166 BARE CR bytes mid-line; Python turns each bare CR into a line break, inflating line numbers by up to 166 versus sed/grep/wc/CI. Measured: LF=29273, CRLF=29273, CR total=29439, bare CR=166; predicted Python lines = 29273+166+1 = 29440 = observed. All line numbers in this file are LF-only and were cross-checked against the Read tool (two independent signals agree).

edge_semantics.HARD: B cannot start until A has produced a named artifact, or B's output is void without A. Violating a hard edge produces rework, not just inefficiency.
edge_semantics.SOFT: B is cheaper/better/safer after A, but B can legitimately start and produce valid output first.

phases.title: Independent confirmation

phases.notes: Requires a severity field on claims to identify 'every P0/P1 claim'. Measured: CLAIM-REGISTRY.json's 10 claims have NO severity field - see COMPLETION-GATES condition 3.

blocked_or_redefined_under_pr_only: marketplace listing (a LIVE public listing is out of scope)
signed artifacts (signing infra tied to publication)
canary install/upgrade/rollback (no canary channel exists in PR-ONLY)
constrained_by_release_mode.owner_decision_needed: Program stop condition 13 is 'release/canary succeeds'. Under PR-ONLY there is no canary. Either (a) redefine condition 13 as 'a merged PR plus a local clean-install/upgrade/rollback rehearsal succeeds', or (b) mark condition 13 permanently N/A under PR-ONLY. Leaving it undefined makes the program unable to ever satisfy its own stopping rule.

phases.title: Self-improvement loop
deliverables: closed loop, 10 steps: observe failure or opportunity; create a structured candidate improvement; reproduce the baseline; implement in isolation; run benchmark and regression suite; independently review; keep ONLY when improvement is measured; revert when neutral or harmful; record the lesson in the correct skill/rule/workflow; update the benchmark so the same failure cannot silently return
constraint: no improvement is retained merely because an agent produced it (line 11150)
phases.notes: UNFUNDED - the only phase with no allocation bucket (see allocation_buckets.FINDING_unfunded_phase). NOT on the critical path to release: 15->16 is SOFT, and the loop's hard deps are the Phase 0 baseline (step 3 'reproduce the baseline') and the Phase 10 benchmark suite (steps 5 and 10).

edges.reason: Phase 1 canonical records carry 'source lineage'; lineage is only stable against a frozen snapshot. Phase 1's 'verification status' field also presupposes Phase 0's known-broken/known-good detector controls.

Phase 2 requires every material claim to carry source lineage, a confidence band and an independent verification path - that is the canonical claim record Phase 1 defines. Researching into an undefined record format yields un-mergeable output. CONTESTED: see blocked_now.CONTESTED-1.
2A searches 'prior artifacts, transcripts' for candidates; Phase 1 is what canonicalized them. Without it, 2A re-discovers duplicates it cannot collapse.
2A runs its own archaeology sweep and can share the Phase 2 research rail concurrently; it consumes no Phase 2 artifact.
Council design is informed by canonical records but the spec itself enumerates the required topologies, protocols and 24 presets, so 2C is self-sufficient to start.
External research on deliberation protocols improves 2C but is not consumed as an artifact.
2B step 1 is literally 'ingest and normalize candidate workflows'. You cannot fuse what has not been acquired.
Benchmark-case selection for fusion evaluation is better informed by Phase 2, but 2B can use in-repo cases.
An architecture tournament with no external research produces nine drafts of the same in-house intuition. The 9 named architectures are research-grounded positions.
Fusion results inform the distributed-workflow-runtime and marketplace-first candidates but are not required to author them.
Council design informs the UX/product-first and maximal-hybrid candidates only.
Contracts are specified FOR the winning architecture. Specifying 20 contracts against an unchosen architecture locks the loser's shape and is thrown away.
Spec line 10822 is explicit: 'Write executable conformance tests before broad implementation.' Phase 5 is broad implementation, gated by the plugin-manifest and permission-model contracts.
Marketplace manifest, package metadata, provenance and permission contracts are Phase 4 outputs the marketplace implements.
The workflow DSL contract is a Phase 4 output; the typed workflow system implements it.
7A requires a VALIDATED CouncilSpec; validation is against the Phase 4 schema contracts.
The skill contract and MCP adapter contract define what the router indexes and how it injects.
Cross-vendor coordination is built on the cross-vendor adapter contract plus the shared work-unit and artifact schemas - all Phase 4 outputs.
The spec mandates a 'test fixture marketplace' (line 10871), which is exactly the decoupling that lets the marketplace be built before a finished plugin exists.

Seeded regression class at line 11331 - 'workflow discovery ignores an existing superior workflow and rebuilds it' - is only preventable with the 2A candidate registry in hand before authoring the 96.
Phase 7's 96 shipped definitions are 2B's certified output; 2B owns certification, lineage and the outperform-or-complement test.
7A productionizes the typed CouncilSpec that 2C designs.
7A implements the council as 'a first-class workflow type', which requires Phase 7's workflow type system to exist.
The router indexes workflows among skills/plugins/tools, but can index skills and tools first and add workflows later.
Test layer 33 (benchmark regression) has no comparator without the Phase 0 pre-change benchmark baselines. Spec line 10656: 'Capture benchmark baselines before changing behavior.'
Test layers 5-8 (clean-install, upgrade, rollback, uninstall) execute Phase 5's install tooling.
Test layer 31 (malicious-plugin) and the marketplace-abuse classes execute Phase 6's registry and permission surface.
Resume, replay, partial-artifact and duplicate-dispatch layers exercise Phase 7's runtime.
Deliberation-calibration units in bucket B08 test the Phase 7A council runtime.
Phase 8's own deliverable is a router regression suite, which is executed here.
Concurrency, crash-recovery, stale-monitor and duplicate-dispatch layers exercise Phase 9's coordination layer.
Confirmers must 'reproduce the baseline failure' and 'reproduce the corrected behavior' - both require the tests to exist and to have run.
Canonical claim records are the refutation targets; there is nothing to refute before they exist.
Most refuter tracks can run on claims alone; only the benchmark-gaming and performance tracks hard-require Phase 10 output.
Refuters are stronger against confirmed claims but must not wait on confirmation - and must default to REFUTED on insufficient evidence.
Blind-spot review asks what was dropped from the canonical corpus; without the corpus the question has no domain.
'What test could falsely pass' and 'what platforms were never tested' are far sharper after Phase 10.
Confirmation discrepancies feed the blind-spot list.
Refutation output feeds 'what failures were normalized away'.
Meta-review must check 'claims of completion not backed by the shared predicate' - it needs confirmer verdicts.
Meta-review must check for 'omitted dissent'; dissent originates in refutation.
The root-cause hierarchy must account for residual risks and accepted blind spots.
Release notes must be 'grounded in verified changes' and promotion requires independent sign-off (line 11133), both Phase 14 outputs.
Loop step 3 is 'reproduce the baseline' - the Phase 0 baseline is the reference.
Loop steps 5 and 10 run and then UPDATE the benchmark and regression suite built in Phase 10.
The loop can observe failures pre-release; it does not consume a release artifact.

critical_path.method: Longest chain of HARD edges only, computed over the 21 phase nodes. SOFT edges are excluded because by definition they can be violated without rework.

edge_reasoning.why_on_path: Nothing can be canonicalized against a moving corpus; Phase 0 is the only source of a frozen snapshot and of the detector controls that make 'verification status' meaningful.

Phase 2's per-claim lineage/confidence/verification-path requirement is the Phase 1 record. CONTESTED - if the claim schema is pulled forward from Phase 4 this edge becomes SOFT and the critical path shortens by one node while releasing 224 units to start today.
The nine committed architectures must be research-grounded, not nine restatements of one in-house intuition.
Contracts are written for the WINNING architecture. Writing 20 contracts before the tournament locks the loser's shape.
Spec line 10822 mandates executable conformance tests before broad implementation; the workflow DSL contract gates the workflow runtime.
The council is specified as a first-class workflow TYPE, so it cannot exist before the workflow type system does.

The deliberation-calibration test units cannot execute against a runtime that does not exist. 7A is the LAST of the six implementation phases to become testable, which is what puts it on the path rather than 5, 6, 8 or 9.
Confirmers reproduce baseline failure and corrected behavior - both require executed tests.
Meta-review checks completion claims against the shared predicate, which requires confirmer verdicts.
Release notes must be grounded in verified changes and promotion requires independent sign-off.

runner_up_paths.note: The workflow-archaeology route. One node shorter, so slack of exactly 1 hop versus the critical path - it is a NEAR-critical path and should be scheduled as if critical.

off_critical_path.16: Hangs off 10 (HARD) and 15 (SOFT). Post-release; not on the path to release.
off_critical_path.6: 4->6->10, one hop shorter than the 7/7A branch.

blocked_now.name: Option-ID collision (finding F-B-02)
blocked_now.detail: 31 option IDs resolve to TWO UNRELATED MEANINGS depending on which artifact is open. 07-OPTION-UNIVERSE family M has 33 ids; 13-ARCHITECTURE-CANDIDATES section 4 mechanism options has 38 ids; they share the M-NN namespace; 31 collide. A further 7 doc-13 ids (M-12, M-16, M-17, M-19, M-28, M-30, M-38) resolve to ABSENT in the universe. Six of the seven ids in doc 13's own owner-decision table mis-resolve.
